title: Understanding XSS and CSRF
description: Learn what XSS and CSRF attacks are and how they affect full-stack apps.

data.text: XSS and CSRF are two of the most common web security vulnerabilities. Understanding them is the first step to protecting your application.

XSS occurs when an attacker injects malicious scripts into content that is then served to other users. The attacker's code runs in the victim's browser with the same permissions as the legitimate site.

data.title: XSS Types
items: Stored XSS: Malicious script is saved on the server and served to all users
Reflected XSS: Script comes from the current HTTP request
DOM-based XSS: Vulnerability exists in client-side JavaScript

data.text: CSRF tricks a logged-in user into executing unwanted actions on a different site. The browser automatically includes cookies with the request, making it appear legitimate.

data.title: Real-World Impact
data.text: XSS can steal session tokens or redirect users. CSRF can transfer money, change passwords, or delete accounts without user knowledge.

cards.title: XSS
cards.description: Attacker injects code into the page. Runs in the user's browser.

cards.title: CSRF
cards.description: Attacker tricks the user's browser into making a request. Exploits trusted cookies.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: CSRF forces unwanted actions via cookies
Both require server and client defenses
data.takeaway: Next, we'll learn how to prevent XSS attacks in your application.
